title: The Three Daughters and the Camels (TE)
summary: A deceased merchant leaves seventeen camels to be divided among three daughters in impossible fractions. Birbal solves the mathematical paradox.
full_text:
A wealthy camel trader of Agra passed away, leaving behind seventeen fine Arabian camels and three grown daughters. His unusual will specified:

'My eldest daughter shall receive one-half (1/2) of my camels.

'My second daughter shall receive one-third (1/3) of my camels.

'My youngest daughter shall receive one-ninth (1/9) of my camels.

'However, no camel may be slaughtered, sold, or cut into pieces; the animals must be divided whole and alive!'

The three daughters and their husbands argued for weeks. Seventeen could not be divided by two (it gave 8 and a half camels)! Seventeen could not be divided by three (it gave 5 and two-thirds)! Seventeen could not be divided by nine!

The disputes grew so bitter that the case was brought before Emperor Akbar. The royal mathematicians and astronomers spent two days writing formulas in the sand, but confessed that seventeen could not be factored into whole numbers without slaughtering a camel.

Akbar turned to Birbal: 'Can this mathematical knot be untangled?'

Birbal smiled: 'With absolute ease, Your Majesty.'

Birbal ordered his own fine riding camel brought from the stables and placed among the seventeen camels of the sisters, making a total of eighteen camels!

Birbal then addressed the daughters:

'Now let us execute your father's will with mathematical precision.

'Eldest daughter, your share is one-half of the camels. One-half of eighteen is nine! Take your nine camels!' The eldest daughter happily took nine camels.

'Second daughter, your share is one-third of the camels. One-third of eighteen is six! Take your six camels!' The second daughter took six camels.

'Youngest daughter, your share is one-ninth of the camels. One-ninth of eighteen is two! Take your two camels!' The youngest daughter took two camels.

The three sisters counted their camels: nine plus six plus two equals seventeen camels!

Every sister had received more than her theoretical share, and all seventeen camels of their late father were divided whole and alive!

Birbal then stepped forward, took the reins of the one remaining eighteenth camel—his own animal—and rode back to his seat with a bow:

'And here is my camel, returned to me untouched!'

The entire court erupted in thunderous applause. Akbar was spellbound by the elegance of the solution, praising Birbal for proving that an outside perspective can effortlessly dissolve what rigid arguments declare impossible.
